title: NOTICE OF REMOVAL TO FEDERAL COURT
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS

CAUSE NO. 3:24-CV-00123-BH

DEBORAH BRYANT, individually and as Representative of the Estate of Marcus Lee, deceased, Plaintiff,
v.
TRITON REFINING COMPANY, LLC, and JASON HARPER, individually, Defendants.

NOTICE OF REMOVAL

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

Pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a), Defendant Triton Refining Company, LLC, a citizen of Delaware, hereby removes the above-entitled and numbered civil action from the 191st Judicial District Court of Dallas County, Texas, to this Court. The original state court action was filed on January 15, 2024, styled as Deborah Bryant v. Triton Refining Company, LLC and Jason Harper, Cause No. DC-24-00321, in the 191st Judicial District Court of Dallas County, Texas.

I. BACKGROUND

Plaintiff Deborah Bryant, a Texas resident, alleges that on or about October 12, 2023, her deceased husband Marcus Lee, while employed as a contractor at Triton's facility located at 4500 Industrial Parkway, Dallas, Texas, suffered fatal injuries due to a chemical explosion. Plaintiff names as defendants Triton Refining Company, LLC, the facility owner, and Jason Harper, a shift supervisor employed by Triton. Plaintiff asserts claims of negligence, gross negligence, and premises liability. Plaintiff's Original Petition was served on Triton on February 1, 2024, and on Harper on February 5, 2024. Removal is timely filed within thirty days of service.

II. GROUNDS FOR REMOVAL

This Court has original jurisdiction pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a) because the matter in controversy exceeds $75,000 exclusive of interest and costs, and the parties are completely diverse. Plaintiff Deborah Bryant is a citizen of Texas. Defendant Triton Refining Company, LLC is a limited liability company whose sole member is Triton Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business in Wilmington, Delaware. Defendant Jason Harper is a citizen of Texas. However, Harper is improperly joined because he was acting within the scope of his employment at all material times, and no viable claim against him exists under Texas law. See, e.g., Great Plains Trust Co. v. Morgan Stanley Dean Witter & Co., 313 F.3d 305 (5th Cir. 2002). Accordingly, his citizenship is disregarded for diversity purposes. The amount in controversy exceeds $75,000, as Plaintiff seeks damages for pain and suffering, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses.

III. STATE COURT DOCUMENTS

Attached as Exhibit A is a true and correct copy of the state court docket sheet, Bates range BRY000001 through BRY000015. As the Court observed in a similar context, "[Bryant] presented sufficient evidence of negligence to survive summary judgment." But here, the federal forum is proper.

IV. APPLICABLE STATUTE

Removal is governed by 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a), which provides: "Except as otherwise expressly provided by Act of Congress, any civil action brought in a State court of which the district courts of the United States have original jurisdiction, may be removed by the defendant or the defendants, to the district court of the United States for the district and division embracing the place where such action is pending."

V. CONCLUSION

For the foregoing reasons, Defendant Triton Refining Company, LLC respectfully requests that this Court accept jurisdiction and proceed accordingly.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Amanda Carter

I certify that a true copy of this Notice was served on counsel for Plaintiff, Sarah Mitchell of Mitchell & Perez, P.C., 200 Commerce Street, Dallas, Texas 75202, via email to smitchell@mitchellperez.com on February 20, 2024.

/s/ Amanda Carter

title: NOTICE OF REMOVAL BY DEFENDANT FEDERAL BANK
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE WESTERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS

CAUSE NO. SA-24-CV-00456-XR

SANDRA COLLINS, Plaintiff,
v.
FEDERAL BANK OF AUSTIN, N.A., Defendant.

NOTICE OF REMOVAL

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

Defendant Federal Bank of Austin, N.A. ("Federal Bank"), a national banking association organized under the laws of the United States, with its main office in Austin, Texas, hereby removes the above-captioned action from the 250th Judicial District Court of Travis County, Texas, to this Court. The original state court petition was filed on March 5, 2024, as Sandra Collins v. Federal Bank of Austin, N.A., Cause No. D-1-GN-24-001234, in the 250th Judicial District Court, Travis County, Texas.

I. FACTUAL BACKGROUND

Plaintiff Sandra Collins, a Texas citizen, alleges that Defendant Federal Bank wrongfully foreclosed on her residential property located at 1200 Elm Street, Austin, Texas. Plaintiff asserts claims for breach of contract, violations of the Texas Debt Collection Act, and negligent misrepresentation. Collins served Federal Bank with citation on March 12, 2024. Removal is timely.

II. DIVERSITY JURISDICTION

This Court has original jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1332. Plaintiff Collins is a citizen of Texas. Federal Bank is a national banking association deemed a citizen of the state in which its main office is located, which is Texas. However, because Federal Bank is also a citizen of the United States for purposes of 28 U.S.C. § 1348, removal is proper under the federal officer removal statute, 28 U.S.C. § 1442(a)(1). The amount in controversy exceeds $75,000, as the property is valued at $350,000.

III. REMOVAL PROCEDURE

Copies of all process, pleadings, and orders served on Defendant are attached as Exhibit A, Bates range FB-001 through FB-050. As the judge noted in a similar case, "[Collins] failed to state a claim for which relief can be granted." However, removal is warranted here.

IV. STATUTORY AUTHORITY

28 U.S.C. § 1442(a)(1) provides: "A civil action commenced in a State court against any of the following may be removed by them to the district court of the United States for the district and division embracing the place wherein it is pending: (1) The United States or any agency thereof or any officer (or any person acting under that officer) of the United States or of any agency thereof, sued in an official or individual capacity for any act under color of such office."

V. CONCLUSION

Defendant respectfully requests that this Court accept jurisdiction.

Respectfully submitted,

title: NOTICE OF REMOVAL IN PRODUCT LIABILITY ACTION
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS

CAUSE NO. 4:24-CV-00789-KH

THOMAS RIVERA, Plaintiff,
v.
MEDCORE PHARMACEUTICALS, INC., Defendant.

NOTICE OF REMOVAL

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

Defendant MedCore Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a corporation incorporated under the laws of New Jersey with its principal place of business in Newark, New Jersey, hereby removes this action from the 215th Judicial District Court of Harris County, Texas, to the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas. The original state court petition was filed on April 10, 2024, as Thomas Rivera v. MedCore Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Cause No. 2024-31245, in the 215th Judicial District Court, Harris County, Texas.

I. NATURE OF ACTION

Plaintiff Thomas Rivera, a Texas citizen, alleges that he suffered severe liver damage after using Defendant's prescription drug, HepaClear, which was manufactured and distributed by MedCore. Plaintiff asserts claims of strict product liability, negligence, and breach of implied warranty. Service was effected on MedCore on April 15, 2024. This Notice is timely.

II. JURISDICTIONAL ALLEGATIONS

Plaintiff is a citizen of Texas. MedCore is a citizen of New Jersey. The amount in controversy, including medical expenses and pain and suffering, exceeds $75,000. Therefore, diversity jurisdiction exists under 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a). See also exhibitJohn Doe attached as Exhibit B, which is a report from Dr. Emily Lawson. The report references a prior case, Rivera v. MedCore Pharmaceuticals, Inc., 892 F.3d 711 (5th Cir. 2018), but that case involved different facts.

III. STATE COURT RECORDS

True copies of all state court filings are attached as Exhibit A, Bates range MEDC-0001 through MEDC-0025. In that record, the state court stated, "[Rivera] has not demonstrated causation." However, the federal court should apply a different standard.

IV. STATUTE INVOLVED

The removal statute provides: "Any civil action brought in a State court of which the district courts of the United States have original jurisdiction, may be removed by the defendant or the defendants, to the district court of the United States for the district and division embracing the place where such action is pending." 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a).

V. CONCLUSION

MedCore respectfully requests removal.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Jonathan Pierce

Texas Bar No. 11223344
PIERCE & HARPER, LLP

/s/ Jonathan Pierce

title: NOTICE OF REMOVAL BY FEDERAL OFFICER
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS

CAUSE NO. 6:24-CV-00101-JDL

MARTHA HENDERSON, Plaintiff,
v.
UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR and GARY FOSTER, individually and in his official capacity,
Defendants.

NOTICE OF REMOVAL

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

Defendant Gary Foster, a federal officer, and joined by the United States Department of the Interior, hereby remove this action from the 3rd Judicial District Court of Anderson County, Texas, to this Court. The original state court petition was filed on May 1, 2024, as Martha Henderson v. United States Department of the Interior and Gary Foster, Cause No. CV-24-000567, in the 3rd Judicial District Court, Anderson County, Texas.

I. FACTS

Plaintiff Martha Henderson, a Texas citizen, alleges that on April 2, 2024, Defendant Gary Foster, a Bureau of Land Management officer, negligently operated a government vehicle in the course of his employment, causing a collision that injured Henderson. Henderson sues the Department and Foster in both capacities.

II. REMOVAL UNDER FEDERAL OFFICER STATUTE

This Court has jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1442(a)(1), which permits removal of actions against federal officers for acts under color of office. Foster was acting within the scope of his employment. The United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Texas has certified that Foster was acting in his official capacity. See also Henderson v. Foster, 456 F.3d 789 (5th Cir. 2006), which supports removal in these circumstances.

III. STATE COURT RECORDS

Attached as Exhibit A are the state court documents, Bates range DOI-1000 to DOI-1050. In the state court, the judge noted, "[Foster] may be entitled to immunity." The attachment includes Plaintiff's SSN: 321-54-9876; DOB: 01/14/1990; Policy No. DOI-AUTO-3321; VIN 1FTFW1E57PKF00123.

IV. STATUTORY TEXT

28 U.S.C. § 1442(a)(1) states: "A civil action commenced in a State court against any of the following may be removed by them to the district court of the United States for the district and division embracing the place wherein it is pending: (1) The United States or any agency thereof or any officer (or any person acting under that officer) of the United States or of any agency thereof, sued in an official or individual capacity for any act under color of such office."

V. CONCLUSION

Defendants respectfully request removal.

Respectfully submitted,

title: NOTICE OF REMOVAL – CLASS ACTION
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS

CAUSE NO. 3:24-CV-00345-L

MARCUS WELLS, individually and on behalf of all others similarly situated, Plaintiff,
v.
SUNRISE ENERGY SERVICES, INC., and RICHARD KANE, Defendants.

NOTICE OF REMOVAL

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

Defendant Sunrise Energy Services, Inc., a Texas corporation with its principal place of business in Houston, Texas, and Defendant Richard Kane, a Texas citizen, hereby remove this class action from the 157th Judicial District Court of Harris County, Texas, to this Court. The original state court petition was filed on June 1, 2024, as Marcus Wells v. Sunrise Energy Services, Inc., and Richard Kane, Cause No. 2024-54321, in the 157th Judicial District Court, Harris County, Texas.

I. CLASS ACTION ALLEGATIONS

Plaintiff Marcus Wells, a Texas citizen, brings a putative class action alleging that Defendants engaged in unlawful price gouging during the February 2021 winter storm, in violation of Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 17.46(a). Wells seeks damages on behalf of all Texas residents charged excessive rates. Defendants were served on June 5, 2024.

II. JURISDICTION UNDER CAFA

This Court has jurisdiction under the Class Action Fairness Act, 28 U.S.C. § 1332(d), because the amount in controversy exceeds $5,000,000, and at least one plaintiff is diverse from at least one defendant. Although all parties are Texas citizens, the minimal diversity requirement is met because the class includes non-Texas citizens. The amount in controversy is $10,000,000. See also Wells v. Sunrise Energy Services, Inc., 789 F.3d 567 (5th Cir. 2015), which supports CAFA jurisdiction.

III. STATE COURT RECORDS

Exhibit A contains state court filings, Bates range SUN-2000 through SUN-2050. In the state court, the judge remarked, "[Wells] may amend the complaint." Exhibit A includes: SSN of Plaintiff: 654-32-1098; DOB of Plaintiff: 09/05/1982; Policy No. SUN-CL-7766; VIN 3VWDG7AJ1KM123456.

IV. STATUTE CITED

Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 17.46(a) provides: "False, misleading, or deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce are hereby declared unlawful."

V. CONCLUSION

Defendants respectfully request removal.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Patricia Nguyen

ATTORNEY FOR DEFENDANTS

I served Plaintiff's counsel, David Bryant of Bryant Law Firm, 500 Travis Street, Houston, Texas 77002, via email to dbryant@bryantlawfirm.com on June 12, 2024.

/s/ Patricia Nguyen
